title: Estimate the mean of grouped data
show: histogram of minutes spent on homework with classes 0-10 to 30-40

example.question:
The table shows the number of minutes 20 students spent on homework.
Minutes: 0–10, 10–20, 20–30, 30–40
Number of students: 3, 7, 6, 4
Estimate the mean time.

steps.say: Take the middle of each group. Add the two ends and halve.
Multiply each mid-value $\hl{1}{x}$ by the number of students $f$, then add them up.
Add the frequencies to get the number of students, then divide.

title: Select an appropriate graphical/numerical summary
show: dot plot of 5,6,6,7,8,40 showing the outlier pulling the mean

example.question: Six students are asked how much pocket money they get each week (in euro): $5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 40$. Which average describes a typical student better, the mean or the median? Calculate both and give a reason.
example.final: \text{Median} = 6.5\text{, because the extreme value } 40 \text{ pulls the mean up to } 12

steps.say: Look at the data first. One value, $\hl{1}{40}$, is far bigger than the rest. An extreme value drags the mean up but hardly moves the median.

rows.aside: Five students get $8$ or less. One gets $40$.

steps.say: Add the values and divide by how many there are.
The data is already in order. With six values, the median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th.
The mean of $12$ is bigger than what five of the six students get. The median is not pulled by the $40$.

rows.aside: Use the **median**: the $40$ is extreme, so the mean is not typical.

title: Describe a distribution's shape
show: histogram or dot plot of 1,2,2,3,3,4,5,24 showing a skewed distribution with a long right tail

example.question: The number of text messages sent by eight students in one day is: $1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 24$. Find the mean and the median. What does this tell you about the shape of the distribution?

steps.say: Add all the values and divide by $8$.
The data is in order. With eight values, the median is halfway between the 4th and 5th.
Subtract. A positive difference means the mean sits above the median.
The mean is above the median. The single big value $24$ is a long tail on the right, and it pulls the mean up.

rows.aside: Mean $>$ median, so the distribution is **positively skewed**.

title: Compare data sets with back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots
show: back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot of Week 1 and Week 2 puzzle times

example.question: The times, in seconds, that seven students took to finish a puzzle in two weeks are: Week 1: $28, 35, 21, 47, 33, 24, 42$. Week 2: $36, 22, 31, 18, 38, 29, 23$. Show the data on a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot and compare the two weeks using the median and the range.
example.final: \text{Week 2 was faster (median } 29 < 33\text{) and less spread out (range } 20 < 26\text{)}

steps.say: Use the tens as stems. Put Week 1 leaves on the right and Week 2 leaves on the left, each row in order, smallest next to the stem.

rows.aside: Key: $2 | 3 | 5$ means $32$ seconds in Week 2 and $35$ in Week 1.

steps.say: With seven values, the median is the 4th one in order. Read it off the plot.
The range is the biggest value minus the smallest.
Say what each number shows, in words, about both weeks.

rows.aside: Week 2 is quicker: its median is $4$ seconds lower.
Week 2 is more consistent: its range is $20$, against $26$.

title: Calculate the correlation coefficient (calculator)
show: scatter plot of (1,3),(2,5),(3,4),(4,7),(5,9) showing positive correlation

example.question:
Five students recorded hours of revision $x$ and test mark $y$:
$(1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 4), (4, 7), (5, 9)$.
Find the correlation coefficient $r$, correct to $3$ decimal places, and say what it shows.

steps.say: Put the calculator in statistics mode with two variables. Type the $x$ values in one column and the $y$ values in the other.

rows.aside: Check each column has $5$ entries before going on.

steps.say: Ask the calculator for $\hl{1}{r}$. Do not round until the end.
Round to $3$ decimal places as asked, then say what the sign and size mean.

rows.aside: $r$ is close to $1$: strong positive correlation. More revision goes with higher marks.

title: Draw a line of best fit by eye and predict
show: scatter plot of the eight (hours, mark) points with the line of best fit drawn

example.question:
The table shows hours of study $x$ and test mark $y$ for eight students.
$(1, 13), (2, 17), (3, 19), (4, 25), (5, 27), (6, 31), (7, 37), (8, 39)$
A line of best fit drawn by eye passes through $(2, 16)$ and $(8, 40)$. Find its equation and use it to predict the mark for a student who studies for $6$ hours.

steps.say: Plot the points. Draw a ruler line through the middle of them with points on both sides, passing through the two given points.

rows.aside: The line should follow the trend, not join the first and last point.

steps.say: Use the two points on the line to find its $\hl{1}{\text{slope}}$.
Put the slope and the point $(2, 16)$ into $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$.
Substitute $x = 6$ into the equation. $6$ is inside the data, so the prediction is reliable.
